item.title: : Federation Council of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation On September 22, Federation Council Speaker
item.description: Federation Council of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation : 🇷🇺 🇿🇼 On September 22, Federation Council Speaker Valentina Matviyenko met with President of the Senate of Zimbabwe Mabel Chinomona . Russia's Federation Council Speaker thanked Zimbabwean parliamentarians for monitoring the State Duma elections . 💬 Valentina Matviyenko noted that the traditionally friendly relations between Russia and Zimbabwe date back to Zimbabwe’s struggle for independence : It is gratifying that Zimbabwe remembers the support our country provided during its difficult struggle for national liberation. We stand ready to continue working closely together to combat neocolonialism . 💬 Russia's Federation Council Speaker emphasised that our countries share common views on the contemporary world order: We oppose interference in the affairs of sovereign states and uphold the leading role of the UN and the primacy of international law. #RussiaZimbabwe

item.title: : Government of the Russian Federation On September 22, ahead of the XII St Petersburg International United Cultures Forum
item.description: Government of the Russian Federation : On September 22, ahead of the XII St Petersburg International United Cultures Forum , Culture Minister Olga Lyubimova met with her counterparts from the DPRK and Thailand. 🇷🇺 🇰🇵 During her meeting with DPRK Culture Minister, Comrade Hyon Un-chol , Olga Lyubimova discussed cooperation in filmmaking and exchanges between museums. The ministers also reviewed cultural cooperation in 2025, including the participation of Russian performing arts groups in the April Spring Friendship Art Festival in Pyongyang. 🇷🇺 🇹🇭 Olga Lyubimova’s meeting with Thailand's Culture Minister Sabida Thaised focused on the flagship international cultural project Russian Seasons , which is currently enjoying a successful run in the Kingdom. Another key topic was preparations to celebrate the 130th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Russia and Thailand in 2027. #RussiaDPRK #RussiaThailand

🎙
Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov's
remarks
at
the “Dialogue on Fakes 4.0” Forum
(Moscow, September 22, 2026)
Key points
:
•
Russia encourages professional dialogue in virtually every field, including efforts to counter the use of information as a weapon.
This is particularly relevant today, when information floods every aspect of our lives and modern technology allows any news story, even one that is unverified or outright false, to reach millions, if not billions, of people almost instantly.
•
I consider
the staged killing of civilians in Bucha
, a suburb of Kiev,
to be the most cynical farce
. Russian troops
withdrew
from the Kiev Region on March 30, 2022. Two days later,
the town’s mayor appeared on television
, proudly declaring that Ukraine had regained full control of Bucha and that no Russian soldiers remained there. The footage was filmed on the town’s main street.
It is a wide street, and it was completely empty.
Yet three days after our units withdrew, a BBC crew appeared there and broadcast a report showing that very same street, with dozens of bodies neatly laid out along its sides, dressed in remarkably clean clothes despite the mud and slush all around.
•
Anti-Russian hysteria was whipped up. New sanctions were announced as punishment.
As you know, then British PM
Boris Johnson
arrived, forbade the signing of the Istanbul peace accords and proposed
simply continuing the wa
r. He recently claimed that this was a lie. Well, he will say anything, and for next to nothing.
But this is no lie – it is the truth.
• In response to the accusations against us and the sanctions,
we simply requested the names
of those whose bodies had been shown by the BBC, which had
“conveniently turned up”
in the right place at the right time.
Complete silence.
•
I appealed to UN Secretary-General Guterres
,
both in private meetings and publicly at a Security Council meeting he attended
, asking him to use his authority and the means at his disposal to secure the publication of the names of those whose alleged deaths at the hands of Russian servicemen had caused such an enormous scandal.
There was no response.
•
We have continued to pursue this matter.
Every year, I remind Guterres that he ought to explain to the international community – or at least to Russia, which has been accused of every imaginable sin – what actually happened there and whose bodies were shown. In May this year, I sent Guterres
12 very specific questions about the Bucha incident
. Guterres responded to my letter containing these 12 specific questions with
a perfunctory reply
.
• Just a few days ago,
The International Public Tribunal on the Crimes of Ukrainian Neo-Nazis published the initial findings of its investigation
.
They were announced and presented on September 17
at the TASS press centre, with the participation of the Tribunal’s Chairman and member of Russia’s Civic Chamber
Maxim Grigoryev
.
👉
Read the full report
• Based solely on open sources – let me stress that again – it has been established that
the memorial bears
dozens of names of Ukrainian armed forces servicemen
, Security Service of Ukraine personnel, members of “territorial defence” units, the police and the National Guard, including militants from the nationalist Azov formation.
More than 70 names have no digital footprint whatsoever,
which is virtually impossible in today’s world.
❗️
I have no doubt that the truth will ultimately prevail
, providing a fitting response to the West’s information aggression against the countries of the Global Majority. Russia is one of them. I would also like to make a very important point. The West’s efforts to conceal and distort the truth in the information sphere reflect a broader trend –
a fear of fair competition in virtually every field of human endeavour.

item.title: 🇷🇺 On September 22, President of Russia Vladimir Putin and Crown Prince, Chairman of the Council of Ministers of Saudi Arabia Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇸🇦 📞 On September 22, President of Russia Vladimir Putin and Crown Prince, Chairman of the Council of Ministers of Saudi Arabia Mohammed bin Salman Al Saud had a telephone conversation . Vladimir Putin congratulated the Crown Prince on the upcoming Saudi National Day , noting that 100 years ago, the Soviet Union became the first foreign state to recognise the Saudi Kingdom . 📈 Both Sides expressed satisfaction with the level of cooperation achieved in political, trade, economic and humanitarian affairs. The Leaders held an in-depth exchange of views on developments in the Middle East , particularly the Persian Gulf. They stressed that there is no alternative to political and diplomatic efforts to resolve the current crisis, with due regard for the interests of all parties. Given the deteriorating military and political situation in Yemen , they reaffirmed the need to end hostilities as soon as possible and create conditions for constructive dialogue among Yemeni parties under UN auspices. They also emphasised the importance of ensuring safe and unimpeded passage for vessels through the region’s international waterways , including the Bab el-Mandeb and Hormuz straits. 🤝 The Leaders agreed to maintain contacts at various levels. #RussiaSaudiArabia
